summary: Iteration 4 backend testing for Pump.fun bot v4 — two new features: (1) POST /api/wallet/send (withdraw SOL with validation), and (2) Re-entry on winners config + watchlist endpoints. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_pump_bot_v4.py with 16 tests across 4 classes — all 16 PASSED (100%). Coverage: (a) /api/wallet/send rejects invalid address (gibberish & empty) with 400 + 'invalid recipient address: ...'; (b) rejects amount_sol=0 and amount_sol<0 with 400 + 'amount_sol must be > 0'; (c) rejects self-send (recipient == bot wallet pubkey) with 400 + 'cannot send to self'; (d) wallet has 0 SOL so a valid foreign recipient + positive amount path hits the balance check and returns 400 + 'insufficient balance' (NOT 500) — verifying the ValueError-to-HTTPException(400) mapping; (e) Pydantic body validation returns 4xx for missing fields; (f) GET /api/bot/config now exposes reentry_enabled, reentry_max_attempts, reentry_pullback_pct, reentry_window_seconds, reentry_size_multiplier with correct types; (g) PUT /api/bot/config clamps reentry_max_attempts to 0..5 (tested 99 -> 5 and -3 -> 0); (h) PUT /api/bot/config persists arbitrary reentry values and GET returns them (test restores baseline after); (i) GET /api/reentry/watchlist returns a list (empty in default paper-mode); (j) DELETE /api/reentry/watchlist/{mint} returns 404 'not on watchlist' for non-existent mint; (k) sanity: /api/ root and /api/bot/status still respond 200 with the expected shape. Regression: ran the full prior 47-test suite (test_pump_bot_api.py + test_pump_bot_enhancements.py + test_pump_bot_v3.py) — 46/47 PASSED, the single failure is the pre-existing TestSocialScoreAvailability::test_some_launch_has_nonzero_social_score (DuckDuckGo 202 from cluster IP — documented in iteration_2 & iteration_3, NOT a v4 regression). WebSocket broadcast paths for reentry_watch_add/remove are wired through hub.broadcast and do not crash the broadcaster (verified indirectly: /api/ws status broadcaster keeps running cleanly throughout the 2m37s regression run with no logged exceptions).

minor.issue: test_some_launch_has_nonzero_social_score still fails because DuckDuckGo IA API returns HTTP 202 with no payload from the cluster IP. Pre-existing from iteration_2; unrelated to v4.

action_items: (Carry-over from iteration_3) Make TestSocialScoreAvailability::test_some_launch_has_nonzero_social_score tolerant of DDG 202 days (skip when DDG returns no abstract/heading across all sampled launches). Not blocking.
critical_code_review_comments: wallet_send.py L17 — send_sol() does NOT verify the bot wallet has a usable keypair before fetching balance; if WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY is missing the call will raise from get_keypair() with a 500 instead of a friendly 400. Acceptable for now (env always set), but consider catching at the route and returning 503.

wallet_send.py L32-39 — balance check uses get_sol_balance() (RPC roundtrip) on every send attempt. For a UI 'preview/dry-run' button consider caching, or add a separate /api/wallet/send/preview endpoint that returns expected fees and remaining balance without submitting a tx.

wallet_send.py L14 FEE_BUFFER_LAMPORTS=5_000_000 (~0.005 SOL) is hardcoded; if priority_fee_microlamports is bumped substantially via /api/bot/config (currently 500_000 microlamports default = 0.0005 SOL/CU * compute units), the buffer could be insufficient or excessive. Compute the buffer dynamically from priority_fee + 5000 base fee + safety margin, or expose as env var.

server.py L84-101 wallet_send route — broadcasts updated wallet info ONLY on success. On failure the wallet balance is unchanged anyway, but the broadcast call after a successful network send happens BEFORE the tx is confirmed on-chain — meaning a viewer might briefly see stale balance until the next 3s status broadcaster cycle pulls fresh RPC data. Acceptable; just noting.

server.py L110-130 update_config — reentry clamping is correct (0..5). Missing clamps on reentry_pullback_pct (could be negative or >100, both nonsensical), reentry_window_seconds (could be 0 or negative — would make the watcher window meaningless), and reentry_size_multiplier (could be 0 or >1 which would size up rather than down). Recommend adding: reentry_pullback_pct max(0.0, min(95.0, x)), reentry_window_seconds max(10, min(3600, x)), reentry_size_multiplier max(0.0, min(1.0, x)).

server.py L276-282 reentry_remove — returns 404 with detail 'not on watchlist', and broadcasts 'reentry_watch_remove'. Good. Consider also broadcasting on the bot.py auto-expiry path (when window_s elapses) so the UI can drop stale items without polling.

models.py BotConfig — reentry_max_attempts=2 default with reentry_size_multiplier=0.5 means after a 25% pullback the bot re-enters at half size, up to 2 attempts. Make sure bot.py._attempt_reentry checks `if not config.reentry_enabled` early and respects the kill-switch / daily_kill_switch_usd before sizing up additional risk.

wallet_send.py — no idempotency: if the user clicks 'Send' twice quickly, two distinct transactions could be submitted (because send_versioned_tx generates a fresh blockhash). For an MVP this is fine, but consider a short in-process lock keyed by (to, amount) or a UI debounce on the frontend.
seed_data_creation: None persisted. test_put_config_persists_reentry_values mutates /api/bot/config but restores original values in a try/finally. test_put_config_clamps_max_attempts_high persists reentry_max_attempts=5 (clamped from 99) — next test_put_config_persists_reentry_values restores it. Net config delta after suite = none.
context_for_next_testing_agent: v4 features fully verified. Re-run safe: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_pump_bot_v4.py -v`. Full regression (~3 min): `pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v`. Wallet has 0 SOL on Gbp9yFREc9dPvnfSjBmi9udg3UCrMmjZh2rjaPebRPrR — DO NOT attempt actual on-chain sends. The bot is left in paper-mode disabled. Re-entry watchlist is populated only by bot.py._exit() on profitable closes; in the test environment (paper-mode, no real fills) the list stays []. The reentry_watch_add/remove WS events therefore couldn't be observed live, but the broadcast call sites are present in server.py L281 and bot.py — they are simple hub.broadcast() calls with dict payloads which the hub already handles correctly per iteration_3 WS tests.
rca of the issue: n/a — no v4-introduced failures. Pre-existing DDG-202 RCA documented in iteration_3.
